questions.q: Which of the following characteristics is true of algae?
questions.solution: <mark>Algae are chlorophyll-bearing, simple, thalloid, autotrophic and largely aquatic (both freshwater and marine) organisms</mark>. They occur in a variety of other habitats: moist stones, soils and wood. Some of them also occur in association with fungi (lichen) and animals (e.g., on sloth bear). The form and size of algae is highly variable, ranging from colonial forms like Volvox and the filamentous forms like Ulothrix and Spirogyra (Figure 3.1). A few of the marine forms such as kelps, form massive plant bodies.The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

questions.q: Where are members of Phaeophyceae primarily found?
questions.solution: <mark>The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats.</mark> They show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex carbohydrates, which may be in the form of laminarin or mannitol. The vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin. The protoplast contains, in addition to plastids, a centrally located vacuole and nucleus. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf-like photosynthetic organ – the frond. Vegetative reproduction takes place by fragmentation. Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella.

questions.q: What types of sexual reproduction are present in brown algae?
questions.solution: The algae reproduce by vegetative, asexual and sexual methods. Vegetative reproduction is by fragmentation. Each fragment develops into a thallus. Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated (motile) and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size (as in Ulothrix) or non-flagellated (non-motile) but similar in size (as in Spirogyra). Such reproduction is called isogamous. Fusion of two gametes dissimilar in size, as in species of Eudorina, is termed as anisogamous. Fusion between one large, non- motile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus. <mark>Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.</mark> Union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium (oogamous species). The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella. The common forms are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.

questions.solution: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem. questions.q:
Select the incorrect statements for the given figure, choose the correct option:

(i)The gymnosperms (gymnas : naked, sperma : seeds) are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilisation. (ii)The leaves in gymnosperms are well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. (iii)The gymnosperms are heterosporous; they produce diploid microspores and megaspores. (iv)The microspores develop into a male gametophytic generation which is highly elaborate and is confined to only a limited number of cells. (v)The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus. (vi)The nucellus is protected by envelopes and the composite structure is called an ovule. (vii)One of the megaspores enclosed within the megasporangium develops into a unicellular female gametophyte that bears two or more archegonia or female sex organs. (viii)Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.
questions.solution: The leaves in gymnosperms are well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. The gymnosperms are heterosporous; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores. The microspores develop into a male gametophytic generation which is highly reduced and is confined to only a limited number of cells. This reduced gametophyte is called a pollen grain. The megaspore mother cell is differentiated from one of the cells of the nucellus. The nucellus is protected by envelopes and the composite structure is called an ovule. One of the megaspores enclosed within the megasporangium develops into a multicellular female gametophyte that bears two or more archegonia or female sex organs. The multicellular female gametophyte is also retained within megasporangium.Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes.

4. Plantae though earlier classifications placed them in the same kingdom.

questions.solution: Fungi, and members of the Monera and Protista having cell walls have now been excluded from Plantae though earlier classifications placed them in the same kingdom. So, the cyanobacteria that are also referred to as blue green algae are not ‘algae’ any more. The earliest systems of classification used only gross superficial morphological characters such as habit, colour, number and shape of leaves, etc.
questions.subject: Botany

2. Blue green algae are algae
3. Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms are classified under Kingdom Plantae
4. The artificial systems gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics
questions.solution: Cyanobacteria that are also referred to as blue-green algae are not algae anymore. We describe Plantae under Algae, Bryophytes, Pteridophytes, Gymnosperms and Angiosperms. The earliest systems of classification used only gross superficial morphological characters such as habit, colour, number and shape of leaves, etc. They were based mainly on vegetative characters or on the androecium structure (system given by Linnaeus). Such systems were artificial; they separated the closely related species since they were based on a few characteristics. Also, the artificial systems gave equal weightage to vegetative and sexual characteristics;

Such a classification for flowering plants was given by George Bentham and Joseph Dalton Hooker.

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. At present phylogenetic classification systems based on evolutionary relationships between the various organisms are acceptable.
2. This classification system assumes that organisms belonging to the same taxa do not have common ancestors.
3. This system became important when there is no supporting fossil evidence.
4. Numerical Taxonomy which is now easily carried out using computers is based on all observable characteristics
questions.solution: At present phylogenetic classification systems based on evolutionary relationships between the various organisms are acceptable. This assumes that organisms belonging to the same taxa have a common ancestor. We now use information from many other sources too to help resolve difficulties in classification. These become more important when there is no supporting fossil evidence. Numerical Taxonomy which is now easily carried out using computers is based on all observable characteristics. Number and codes are assigned to all the characters and the data are then processed. In this way each character is given equal importance and at the same time hundreds of characters can be considered.

questions.solution: Asexual reproduction is by the production of different types of spores, the most common being the zoospores. They are flagellated and on germination gives rise to new plants. Sexual reproduction takes place through fusion of two gametes. These gametes can be flagellated and similar in size as in Chlamydomonas or non-flagellated and non-motile but similar in size as in Spirogyra. Fusion between one large, nonmotile (static) female gamete and a smaller, motile male gamete is termed oogamous, e.g., Volvox, Fucus.

3. The chloroplasts may be discoid, plate -like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral or ribbon-shaped in different species.

questions.solution: The members of chlorophyceae are commonly called green algae. They are usually grass green due to the dominance of pigments chlorophyll a and b. The chloroplasts may be discoid, plate -like, reticulate, cup-shaped, spiral or ribbon-shaped in different species. Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Pyrenoids contain starch besides protein.
2. Most of the members have one or more storage bodies called Pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts.
3. Some alage may store food in the form of oil droplets.
4. Vegetative reproduction usually takes place by budding or by formation of different types of spores
5. The asexual reproduction shows considerable variation in the type and formation of sex cells and it may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
questions.solution: Most of the members have one or more storage bodies called Pyrenoids located in the chloroplasts. Pyrenoids contain protein besides starch. Some algae may store food in the form of oil droplets. Vegetative reproduction usually takes place by fragmentation or by formation of different types of spores. Asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia. The sexual reproduction shows considerable variation in the type and formation of sex cells and it may be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose
2. Asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia.
3. Some commonly found green algae are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus.
4. The members of chlorophyceae or green algae are found primarily in marine habitats.
questions.solution: Green algae usually have a rigid cell wall made of an inner layer of cellulose and an outer layer of pectose. Asexual reproduction is by flagellated zoospores produced in zoosporangia. Some commonly found green algae are: Chlamydomonas, Volvox, Ulothrix, Spirogyra and Chara. The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The members of phaeophyceae are called brown algae because they possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls.
2. Brown algae are found only in freshwater habitats
3. Food is stored as starch.
4. The vegetative cells have a pectose wall usually covered on the outside by a gelatinous coating of algin.
5. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf like photosynthetic organ – the frond.
questions.solution: The members of phaeophyceae are found primarily in marine habitats. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. Food is stored as mannitol and laminarin. The plant body is usually attached to the substratum by a holdfast, and has a stalk, the stipe and leaf like photosynthetic organ – the frond.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

3. Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anigamous or oogamous.
4. The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella
questions.solution: Asexual reproduction in most brown algae is by biflagellate zoospores that are pear-shaped and have two unequal laterally attached flagella. Sexual reproduction may be isogamous, anigamous or oogamous. Union of gametes may take place in water or within the oogonium. The gametes are pyriform (pear-shaped) and bear two laterally attached flagella
questions.subject: Botany

3. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas.

questions.solution: The common forms of phaeophyceae are Ectocarpus, Dictyota, Laminaria, Sargassum and Fucus. The members of Rhodophyceae are commonly called red algae because of the predominance of the red pigment, r-phycoerythrin in their body. Majority of the red algae are marine with greater concentrations found in the warmer areas.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Rhodophyceae occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates.
2. The red thalli of most of the red algae multicellular
3. The food is stored as mannitol and laminarin.
4. The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation
questions.solution: In Rhodophyceae, they occur in both well-lighted regions close to the surface of water and also at great depths in oceans where relatively little light penetrates. The red thalli of most of the red algae are multicellular. The food is stored as floridean starch which is very similar to amylopectin and glycogen in structure. The red algae usually reproduce vegetatively by fragmentation
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom.
2. They have true roots, stem or leaves.
3. The main plant body of the Bryophyte is diploid.
4. The plant body of bryophytes is less differentiated than that of algae
5. They do not possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures at all.
questions.solution: Bryophytes are also called amphibians of the plant kingdom. They lack true roots, stem or leaves. The main plant body of the Bryophyte is haploid.he plant body of bryophytes is more differentiated than that of algae. It is thallus-like and prostrate or erect, and attached to the substratum by unicellular or multicellular rhizoids. They lack true roots, stem or leaves. They may possess root-like, leaf-like or stem-like structures.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Bryophytes in general are of little economic importance but some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals, birds and other animals.
2. Species of Marchantia, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material
3. Mosses along with Lichens are the first organisms to colonise rocks and hence, are of great ecological importance.
4. The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses.
questions.solution: Bryophytes in general are of little economic importance but some mosses provide food for herbaceous mammals, birds and other animals. Species of Sphagnum, a moss, provide peat that have long been used as fuel, and as packing material for trans-shipment of living material because of their capacity to hold water. The bryophytes are divided into liverworts and mosses.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

1. The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods.
2. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid.
3. Gemma cups are found in Pteridophytes
4. The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals.
5. The sporophyte is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule.
questions.solution: The liverworts grow usually in moist, shady habitats such as banks of streams, marshy ground, damp soil, bark of trees and deep in the woods. The plant body of a liverwort is thalloid. Gemma cups are found in Bryophytes. The gemmae become detached from the parent body and germinate to form new individuals. The sporophyte is differentiated into a foot, seta and capsule.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consist of two stages.
2. The first stage is leafy stage followed by second stage that is protonema.
3. The protonema stage bears the sex organs.
4. Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema.
questions.solution: The predominant stage of the life cycle of a moss is the gametophyte which consists of two stages. The first stage is the protonema stage. The second stage is the leafy stage. This stage bears the sex organs. Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema.
2. In sexual reproduction, the sex organs antheridia and archegonia are produced at the bottom of the leafy shoots.
3. Common examples of Mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum and Sphagnum.
4. The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts.
5. The mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal
questions.solution: Vegetative reproduction in mosses is by fragmentation and budding in the secondary protonema. In sexual reproduction, the sex organs antheridia and archegonia are produced at the apex of the leafy shoots. After fertilisation, the zygote develops into a sporophyte, consisting of a foot, seta and capsule. The sporophyte in mosses is more elaborate than that in liverworts. The capsule contains spores. Spores are formed after meiosis. The mosses have an elaborate mechanism of spore dispersal. Common examples of mosses are Funaria, Polytrichum and Sphagnum.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The Bryophytes include horsetails and ferns.
2. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders.
3. Pteridophytes are also frequently grown as ornamentals.
4. Evolutionarily, they are the last terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.
questions.solution: The Pteridophytes include horsetails and ferns. Pteridophytes are used for medicinal purposes and as soil-binders. They are also frequently grown as ornamentals. Evolutionarily, they are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues – xylem and phloem.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Pteridophytes are the first terrestrial plants to possess vascular tissues - xylem and phloem
2. In Pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves.
3. The root, stem and leaves of Pteridophytes do not contain vascular tissues.
4. In pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves
5. The leaves in pteridophyta are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns.
questions.solution: In Pteridophytes, the main plant body is a sporophyte which is differentiated into true root, stem and leaves. These organs possess well-differentiated vascular tissues. The leaves in pteridophyta are small (microphylls) as in Selaginella or large (macrophylls) as in ferns.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

1. The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia, respectively
2. Water is not required for transfer of antherozoids from antheridia.
3. In Pteridophytes, most of the plants are heterosporus.
4. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods
questions.solution: The gametophytes bear male and female sex organs called antheridia and archegonia, respectively. Water is required for transfer of antherozoids released from the antherozoids. In majority of the Pteridophytes all the spores are of similar kinds, such plants are called homosporus. The female gametophytes in these plants are retained on the parent sporophytes for variable periods
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

2. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to male and female gametophytes, respectively.
3. The Pteridophytes are further classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum); Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum)
4. Fusion of male gamete with the egg present in the archegonium result in the formation of zygote.
5. Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes.
questions.solution: Genera like Selaginella and Salvinia which produce two kinds of spores, macro and micro spores, are known as heterosporus. The megaspores and microspores germinate and give rise to female and male gametophytes, respectively. The Pteridophytes are further classified into four classes: Psilopsida (Psilotum), Lycopsida (Selaginella, Lycopodium), Sphenopsida (Equisetum) and Pteropsida (Dryopteris, Pteris, Adiantum). Fusion of male gamete with the egg present in the archegonium result in the formation of zygote. Zygote thereafter produces a multicellular well-differentiated sporophyte which is the dominant phase of the pteridophytes.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are enclosed by any ovary wall and do not remain exposed, before and after fertilization.
2. The seeds that develop post fertilization, are not covered, i.e. are naked.
3. Gymnosperms include medium-sized trees or tall trees and shrubs.
4. The leaves in gymnosperms are not adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind.
questions.solution: The gymnosperms are plants in which the ovules are not enclosed by any ovary wall and remain exposed, both before and after fertilization. The seeds that develop post fertilization, are not covered i.e. are naked. Gymnosperms include medium-sized trees or tall trees and shrubs. The leaves in gymnosperms are well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:

1. The roots are generally tap roots in gymnosperms.
2. Roots in some genera of gymnosperms have fungal association in the form of mycorrhiza, while in some others, small specialised roots called collaroid roots are associated with N2 - fixing cyanobacteria.
3. The leaves in gymnosperms are not well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind.
4. In conifers, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area.
5. Their thick cuticle and sunken stomata also help to reduce water loss.
questions.solution: The roots in gymnosperms are tap roots. Roots in some genera have fungal association in the form of mycorrhiza, while in some others, small specialised roots called collaroid roots are associated with N2 fixing cyanobacteria. The leaves in gymnosperms are well-adapted to withstand extremes of temperature, humidity and wind. In conifers, the needle-like leaves reduce the surface area. Their thick cuticle and sunken stomata also help to reduce water loss.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. The gymnosperms are heterosporus; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores.
2. In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes have an independent free-living existence.
3. The seeds in gymnosperms are covered.
4. The development of pollen grains take place within the megasporangia.
questions.solution: The gymnosperms are heterosporus; they produce haploid microspores and megaspores. In gymnosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. After fertilization, zygote develops into an embryo and the ovules into seeds. These seeds are not covered. The development of pollen grains take place within the microsporangia.
questions.subject: Botany

questions.q:
Read the following statements and choose the correct option:
1. Unlike the gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in the angiosperms, the pollen grains and ovules are developed in specialised structures called flowers.
2. The dicotyledons are characterised by one cotyledon while the monocotyledons have only two.
3. Angiosperms are divided into two classes: the dicotyledons and the monocotyledons.
4. Unlike bryophytes and pteridophytes, in gymnosperms the male and the female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence.
5. The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards archegonia in the ovules and discharge their contents near the mouth of the archegonia.
questions.solution: Unlike the gymnosperms where the ovules are naked, in the angiosperms, the pollen grains and ovules are developed in specialised structures called flowers. They are divided into two classes: the dicotyledons and the monocotyledons. The dicotyledons are characterised by having two cotyledons in their seeds while the monocotyledons have only one. . The pollen tube carrying the male gametes grows towards archegonia in the ovules and discharge their contents near the mouth of the archegonia.
